info.title: DockPanel Mail API
info.description:
Send and manage mail on a DockPanel host over REST.

Messages are injected through Postfix's local `sendmail` wrapper, so they are DKIM-signed and delivered on exactly the same path as mail sent from the webmail, and a copy is filed into the sender's **Sent** folder.

## Authentication

Every route except `GET /health` requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Two kinds of token are accepted, and only one of them is a *mailbox*:

* **A mailbox token** — minted per-mailbox in Roundcube under **Settings → Mail API**. It may send as its own address and manage only its own mailbox (the `/v1/me/*` routes). This is the token an application should hold.
* **A panel API key** — one beginning with `dp_`, created in the panel under **Settings → API keys**. It is not bound to a mailbox; it authenticates as the panel does, which is what the server-wide `/v1/domains/*` and `/v1/queue/*` routes require.

The two are not interchangeable: a mailbox token gets `403` on a management route, a `dp_` key is refused by nothing but the panel's own authorization — and `GET /v1/me` reports which level the presented token is at, as `admin`.

servers.description: This host (same origin the API is served from)

tags.name: Send
tags.description: Inject an outbound message as the authenticated mailbox.

tags.name: Self-service
tags.description: The caller's own mailbox. Any mailbox token may use these, and only for its own address.

tags.name: Management
tags.description: Server-wide mail administration. Requires a panel `dp_` API key, or a mailbox listed in the service's `MAILAPI_ADMIN_EMAILS`.

post.description: Sends as the mailbox the token belongs to. `from` defaults to that mailbox and is refused if it names any other address (a display name is fine). At least one `to` recipient is required; provide `text` and/or `html`.

200.description: Accepted for delivery. `accepted` lists every envelope recipient, including BCC.

403.description: The token may not send as the requested `from` address.

post.description: Kept for callers written against the original route. Identical to `POST /v1/send`.

403.description: The token may not send as the requested `from` address.

200.description: The authenticated mailbox and its level.

put.description: `null` leaves the display name unchanged; an empty string clears it.

put.summary: Set or clear the forwarding address
put.description: A `PUT` replaces the setting, so an omitted `forward_to` means "no forwarding". An empty string clears it.
Any field left out is left unchanged.

get.description: Usage is read live from Dovecot, so it reflects what has actually been delivered; the limit comes from the panel, where it is configured.

delete.description: The folder is named by a query parameter rather than a path segment because folder names legitimately contain `/`. `INBOX`, `Sent` and `Trash` are structurally protected and are refused.

get.summary: List the messages in a folder
get.description: `Drafts`, `Sent` and `Trash` are folders rather than routes: name one with `folder` and this is how it is read. Newest first.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Folder to read. Defaults to `INBOX`. A query parameter rather than a path segment because folder names legitimately contain `/`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most messages to return. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 500.

post.summary: Append a message to a folder
post.description: Writes a message into a folder without sending it — how a draft is saved. It is built by the same code that `/v1/send` sends with, so it takes the same fields, except that no recipient is required. When the mailbox does not hand the message back, `uid` is `null` and any `flags` were not applied.

delete.description: A delete in mail is a move to `Trash`. `permanent=true` expunges instead, and a message already in `Trash` is expunged either way.

200.description: The message was deleted — moved or expunged, as `moved_to` and `permanent` report.

moved_to.description: Set when the message was moved rather than expunged.

post.summary: Move a message to another folder
post.description: How a message is restored out of `Trash`, or filed into `Sent`.

post.summary: Set the flags on a message
post.description: The flags the mailbox holds afterwards are read back, not predicted: `\Recent` is Dovecot's to set. Only `\Seen`, `\Answered`, `\Flagged`, `\Draft` and `\Deleted` may be set, with or without the leading backslash.

200.description: The message's flags after the change.
How much was in `Trash` when it was emptied.
Every mail domain on the host.

post.description: Creates the domain, its DKIM key, and — when the panel manages the zone — its DNS records.

delete.description: Removes the domain and its mailboxes, and — when the panel manages the zone — the DNS records it created.

put.description: Any of `password`, `display_name`, `quota_mb`, `enabled`, `forward_to`, `autoresponder_enabled`, `autoresponder_subject`, `autoresponder_body`. Fields left out are left unchanged.

200.description: Every alias and forward in the domain.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Alias id, as returned by the alias list.

get.description: What the MTA is holding, and why.

200.description: The message was removed from the queue.

bearerAuth.description: A per-mailbox token minted in Roundcube (Settings → Mail API), or a panel API key beginning with `dp_`. Both travel in the same `Authorization` header.

Email.name: email
Email.description: A full mailbox address inside that domain.

Forbidden.description: The token is valid but is not allowed to perform a server-wide operation.

NotFound.description: No such domain, mailbox, or alias.

Internal.description: The operation failed on the server.

Ok.description: A management call proxied to the panel. The panel's own body is returned; its shape is not restated here.

MessageRequest.description: The parts of a message a caller sets. One schema for both doors, because a message written into a folder is built by the same code that sends one — only the sending differs.

from.description: Sender. Defaults to the token's mailbox, and is refused if it names any other address. A display name (`Name <a@b.c>`) is allowed.

to.description: Primary recipients. Required when sending; a draft may have none.

bcc.description: Blind recipients. They receive the message but never appear in its headers.

html.description: HTML body. With `text` too, the message is sent as multipart/alternative.

SendRequest.description: A message to send. The one difference from `MessageRequest` is `to`: a message may be stored in a folder with no recipient, but it cannot be sent to nobody.

id.description: The message's `Message-ID`, useful as a handle to key on.

admin.description: Whether this token may use the server-wide `/v1/domains/*` and `/v1/queue/*` routes.

forward_to.description: An address to forward to. Omitted or `""` clears forwarding.

used_kb.description: Bytes in use, in KiB, summed over every folder.

quota_mb.description: The limit, from the panel. `null` when no limit is set.

MessageSummary.description: One message, as a listing shows it.

uid.description: Mailbox ordinal. Stable within a folder until the message is expunged.

flags.description: Dovecot's flags for the message, split into a list.

date.description: The `Date` header, as the message wrote it.

total.description: Messages in the folder, before `limit` and `offset`.

text.description: The stored message as it is on disk, headers included.

folder.description: Folder the message is in now.

to.description: Folder to move it to. Both must already exist.

MessageAppend.description: A message written into a folder instead of being sent — how a draft is saved.

folder.description: Folder to write into. The mailbox must already have it, so a typo cannot create one.

flags.description: Flags to set on the stored message. `\Draft` is what makes a saved message a draft.

id.description: The `Message-ID` this server generated for the message.

uid.description: The uid the message was stored as, or `null` when the mailbox did not hand it back — in which case the flags could not be applied either.

add.description: Flags to set. The leading backslash is optional.

flags.description: The flags the mailbox holds after the change, read back rather than predicted.

catch_all.description: Address that receives mail for unknown mailboxes. `""` or null disables it.

email.description: Either the local part (`sales`) or a full address inside the domain.
